extracted.intended_audience: authors and editors of biomedical journals (ICMJE member journals and other medical journals)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for completing and implementing the ICMJE uniform conflict-of-interest disclosure form for biomedical journal submissions, including what to report, form structure, and translation/technical considerations. Intended to standardize reporting across journals and reduce author and reader confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a uniform electronic disclosure form (public domain)
rubrics_metrics.description: ICMJE developed an electronic uniform disclosure form and placed it in the public domain in October 2009; the form is available on the ICMJE website and member journals' sites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single, publicly available standard form is intended to lessen confusion caused by variability among journals, ease the reporting burden on authors, and should be adopted by journals to standardize reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not require disclosure of spouses' and minor children's interests
rubrics_metrics.description: The major change in the form is the removal of the queries about potential competing interests of authors’ spouses and minor children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change responds to commenters who noted immense difficulty in defining competing interests beyond direct exchanges of money; journals should not require authors to report spouses' or minor children's interests on this form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open-ended reporting of nonfinancial and indirect interests (Section 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific questions about nonfinancial competing interests were replaced with a single open-ended query (new Section 4) asking, “Are there any other relationships or activities that readers could perceive to influence, or that give the appearance of potentially influencing, what you wrote in the submitted work?”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This places the onus on the person completing the form to identify and report appropriate nonfinancial competing interests. It is intended to be less intrusive than specific checklists while providing a locus to report indirect or nonfinancial relationships that may be perceived as potential conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary focus on competing interests involving direct exchange of money
rubrics_metrics.description: The Committee continues to define clear competing interests as those that involve the direct exchange of money from an interested party to an individual author or the author’s institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While direct financial exchanges are emphasized, the form still allows authors to report indirect or nonfinancial influences via the open-ended question; the form acknowledges complexity and nuance in nonfinancial influences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity through numeric designation and revised wording
rubrics_metrics.description: Each field now has a numeric designation and the language in the instructions and in the individual queries has been modified for clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numbered fields and clearer wording are intended to improve usability, help non-native English speakers, and reduce ambiguity in responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Glossary and guidance for translation
rubrics_metrics.description: To make the form more useful to non-native English speakers, ICMJE is creating a glossary of terms used in the form and will post guidelines for translating the form’s instructions into multiple languages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translations must capture the essence of the queries rather than their literal meaning; the glossary and translation instructions will be made available on the ICMJE website as they become available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical deployment requirement (Adobe Reader dependency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some technical comments were raised about the correct deployment of the form: it requires the user to download the free Adobe 8.0 Reader or higher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals and users should be aware of and accommodate this technical requirement when implementing or completing the electronic form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition policy for authors who used older form
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors who have completed the older version of the form in conjunction with a journal submission need not complete the new form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The new form will be the standard for new submissions going forward; prior-completed older forms remain acceptable for those submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicit user feedback and iterative revision
rubrics_metrics.description: ICMJE piloted the form, invited feedback from authors, editors and others, and revised the form based on comments; the committee will consider comments received before a set date when preparing the next iteration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The form is intended to be iterative—stakeholders should provide feedback (via the ICMJE contact link) to inform future revisions; expect occasional updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance between comprehensiveness and burden
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledgement that the complexity, subjectivity and emotionality of conflict disclosure means some will find the form excessively burdensome while others will find it insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Committee emphasizes not letting 'the perfect be the enemy of the good'—prioritize a simpler, standardized form that alleviates confusion and reduces reporting burden even if it will not satisfy all stakeholders completely; journals are encouraged to adopt the revised form.
